description: The United Kingdom Minerals Yearbook 2025 is a BGS statistical compilation of minerals production, consumption and trade for the UK, broken down by region where possible. It includes annual tonnages of crushed rock, land-won and marine-dredged sand and gravel, other construction minerals, industrial minerals (for example silica sand, kaolin, ball clay, salt, polyhalite, barytes and fluorspar) and energy minerals (coal, onshore and offshore oil and gas), plus consumption, imports and exports, offshore production, values, the number of quarries and the balance of trade, with commodity tables for each mineral. The 2025 edition was published on 2 April 2026 through the National Geoscience Data Centre as a single Excel workbook (about 512 KB), revised on 29 July 2026 after errors in tabs 33 and 34. Access is open under the Open Government Licence, with the acknowledgement "Contains data supplied by UKRI". Caveats: figures are national and regional aggregates, not site data, and some series depend on industry returns. For simulation it gives the UK production and trade baseline for construction and industrial minerals, useful to size material flows and import dependence in supply chain disruption models. Related catalogue records include BGS World Mineral Statistics, BGS BritPits and the UK mineral processing, refining and recycling facilities dataset.
